description: Sourdough by baker's percentages: hydration, starter, and salt for any flour weight, plus starter feeding and a levain builder.
intro: Sourdough looks like guesswork until you weigh it. Every sourdough formula is the same four numbers: flour, water, starter, and salt, each written as a percentage of the flour. Flour is always 100%. Once you know the percentages, any loaf is arithmetic, and scaling a recipe up or down is just changing the flour weight.

The one number that trips people up is the starter. A starter kept at 100% hydration is half flour and half water by weight, so 100 grams of starter quietly adds 50 grams of flour and 50 grams of water to the dough. These calculators count that flour and water, the way King Arthur Baking and The Perfect Loaf describe it, so the hydration you ask for is the hydration you get.

Start with the hydration that matches your loaf: 60% for a firm, easy dough, 70% for the classic open crumb, 85% for a very wet dough with big holes. The feeding calculator keeps your starter fed at any ratio, the levain builder makes exactly the amount your recipe needs, and the two-loaf and sandwich calculators cover the batches a family actually bakes.
